title: Reader inline pill labels wrap and crowd settings choices
symptom: A long system TTS voice display name in the reader settings sheet could wrap inside a choice pill and push later choices out of the visible area. A Pixel 8 / Android 14 Compose regression reproduced this at 320dp width: the long voice label measured 60dp high before the fix, and the following normal voice choice was not displayed in the constrained settings panel.
root_cause: ReaderInlinePill is shared by settings tabs, reading-mode choices, steppers, and TTS choices, but its Text did not enforce single-line overflow behavior. Variable labels from the system voice catalog could therefore expand the pill height instead of being ellipsized like other reader chrome labels.
fix: Constrained ReaderInlinePill labels to one line.
Rendered overflowing shared pill labels with TextOverflow.Ellipsis and disabled soft wrapping.
Added a Compose instrumented regression with a long TTS system voice name and a normal voice choice in a 320dp-wide settings panel.
failed_attempts: Fixing only the TTS voice choice wrapper would leave the same wrapping risk in settings tabs, reading-mode choices, and stepper pills that reuse ReaderInlinePill.
Comparing a padded pill's semantics bounds against an unpadded section title is too strict; compare long and normal pill bounds instead.
impact: Keeps shared reader setting controls stable with long labels, preserves choice density, and prevents later options from being visually crowded out.
